summary: DAY cumulative falsification covered all 12 Chief-selected active-batch companies. No thesis is presently falsified outright. The strongest live challenge set is customer concentration, capital intensity/dilution, acquisition/integration risk, AI-capex common-factor exposure, and policy/technology substitution. These risks are sufficiently identified for conservative Chief treatment in this lane; they are not generic reasons for indefinite non-readiness. All 12 are advisory ready_for_chief from the adversarial lane, while underwriting/source/global discovery gates remain independent.

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Large Meta/Microsoft-style capacity commitments validate demand but create concentration, delivery and financing dependence; headline contract value must not substitute for realized cluster margins or capital efficiency.
unknowns: Normalized cluster margins, utilization and termination economics

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Government/defense demand can be lumpy and politically exposed; rapid revenue growth does not eliminate receivables, backlog-conversion or funding-cycle risk.
unknowns: Backlog conversion and long-run commercial diversification

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Pre-commercial nuclear execution remains the core falsifier: equity-funded liquidity can coexist with absent proven unit economics, licensing slippage and future construction-capital needs.
unknowns: Realized offtake economics, licensing timing and plant capex

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Self-mining, ASIC and AI-infrastructure ambitions compete for capital; leverage and dilution can mask whether AI Cloud creates superior returns versus mining exposure.
unknowns: Fully diluted overhang and segment-level normalized returns

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Q1 2026 operating loss was $271.5M and operating cash use $151M; acquisitions including SkyWater increase vertical capability but also integration, headcount, stock-compensation and capital intensity before broad quantum advantage is proven.
unknowns: Post-SkyWater integration cost, sustainable gross margin and timing of broad quantum advantage

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: One customer represented 90.5% of quarterly revenue and 82.8% of accounts receivable at June 27, 2026. This is an extreme, disclosed concentration risk: deployment pauses, pricing pressure or insourcing by that customer would materially impair results.
unknowns: Customer diversification pace and economics of next-wave deployments

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Top-ten customers represented 82% of fiscal-2026 revenue and two customers exceeded 10%; AI/custom-silicon upside therefore coexists with hyperscaler/distributor concentration, design-win volatility and export-policy exposure.
unknowns: Customer-specific design-win duration and margin mix

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: NVIDIA's $2B equity investment and purchase commitment improve capacity funding and demand visibility but increase strategic/customer dependence; Coherent also carries about $3.2B of debt and significant goodwill sensitivity.
unknowns: NVIDIA-linked revenue concentration, capacity-ramp yields and goodwill downside under AI demand normalization

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Two end customers represented 26.6% and 15.0% of fiscal-2026 revenue and receivables were also concentrated; optical demand strength can reverse abruptly with architecture transitions, customer insourcing or capex resets.
unknowns: Identity/economics of concentrated customers and architecture-transition share retention

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Enterprise-data revenue grew 164.3% year over year on AI/server power demand, creating a favorable but increasingly AI-capex-sensitive mix. The failure case is design-share loss or a datacenter power-architecture transition faster than product conversion.
unknowns: AI customer concentration and durable share in 800V architectures

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Q2 growth is exceptional, but HPS/CCS concentration in AI infrastructure plus an August $3B equity offering creates a classic capacity-cycle risk: capital is being added into very high expectations, so utilization and customer concentration must be stress-tested.
unknowns: Top-customer concentration, use-of-proceeds returns and downside utilization under capex normalization

perCompanyCoverage.challenge: Amphenol completed roughly $10.7B of acquisitions in H1 2026 including CommScope, funded partly with new debt. Organic growth is strong, but leverage, integration, purchase-accounting noise and China tax issues can reduce apparent diversification benefits.
unknowns: Post-CommScope synergy realization, normalized leverage and acquisition-adjusted return on capital

materialFindings.finding: The current batch has unusually high common-factor exposure to AI infrastructure spending across NBIS, MRVL, COHR, LITE, MPWR, CLS and APH; ticker count overstates economic diversification.
SYM is the clearest disclosed single-company concentration outlier: one customer was 90.5% of quarterly revenue and 82.8% of receivables at June 27, 2026.

IONQ, OKLO and BTDR demonstrate a shared anti-pattern: large strategic optionality can coexist with material cash burn, dilution/capital needs and unproven unit economics; optionality must not inflate quality without realized evidence.
COHR and APH both gained strategically important assets/capital in 2026, but the red-team counterweight is balance-sheet/integration risk rather than assuming all inorganic growth is moat accretion.

contradictions: Customer commitments and strategic equity investments can simultaneously validate demand and increase dependency/concentration.
Strong AI-linked growth can improve current margins while increasing sensitivity to a synchronized hyperscaler-capex reset.
Acquisitions can expand moat and manufacturing capability while increasing debt, integration risk and accounting complexity.
unknowns: Exact customer identities/economics remain undisclosed for several optical/semiconductor names.
A standardized common-factor stress model is not yet canonical across the active batch.
Live valuation is intentionally not used to determine red-team baseline readiness.

peerRequests.request: Encode disclosed concentration and capital-structure facts reproducibly, especially SYM, MRVL, LITE, COHR, CLS and APH; do not treat future falsifiers as perpetual blockers when current evidence supports conservative risk treatment.
Preserve shared AI-capex/common-customer factor risk at reconciliation so company-count diversification does not inflate confidence.

accuracyDebates.reason: Explicit shared-factor treatment reduces false diversification confidence without changing locked methodology weights.
